pages.title: WB57 History
pages.text: WB57 History A Brief History of the B-57 Canberra The inception of the B-57 dates back to 1944, when World War II brought English Electric Company Ltd back into the business of designing airplanes. The company had gotten out of the design business in 1926, but with the dawn of the jet engine, the company decided to answer a proposal sent out by the Ministry of Aircraft Production. The first test flight of the B-57 Canberra was May of 1949. The United States Air Force first got interested in the Canberra, as well as many other aircraft, in 1950 when it was looking for a replacement for the aging Douglas B-26 Invader. The Air Force was to make its final selection for the replacement aircraft after a final demonstration in February of 1951. The B-57 was flown in by the Royal Air Force for the demonstration, making the flight across the Atlantic in four hours and forty minutes, setting an unofficial record time for the crossing in either direction. This was also the first unrefuelled Atlantic crossing by any jet-powered aircraft. Coming into the demonstration flight with such fan-fare, the Canberra easily stole the show, and won the contract. Throughout the lifespan of the B-57, there were several variations of the aircraft, ranging from an "A" model to an "F" model. The B-57 also had two prefixes, an "R" designating it a reconnaissance plane, and a "W" designation for weather. A total of 21 "F" models were constructed by modifying existing B-57s. pages.title: WB57 Lifes Support
pages.text: WB57 Lifes Support Life Support The WB-57 is capable of flying at altitudes well over 60,000 feet. Twelve miles high, the environment is very inhospitable to people. In fact, there is less than 1 psi of atmospheric pressure and temperatures will approach -70° F. For these reasons, flight rules mandate that for flight above 50,000 feet, all crewmembers must wear a full pressure suit. If the cabin were to depressurize, or the crew was forced to eject, it would be the only means of survival. Above 10,000 feet, atmospheric pressure becomes low enough that without breathing 100% oxygen, the average person will become hypoxic (an oxygen deprived state) and can eventually lose consciousness. Photo of a Pressure suit As altitude increases, the Time of Useful Consciousness (TUC) becomes shorter. The TUC at 60,000 feet is only 9 - 12 seconds. The TUC can be pushed much higher if 100% oxygen is breathed. At a height of 35,000 feet, the pressure is approximately 20% that of sea level, and since oxygen is approximately 20% of air, a person at this altitude breathing pure oxygen will receive a sea level equivalent amount of oxygen. At heights above 50,000 feet, even with 100% oxygen, a person will quickly become hypoxic, because the ambient pressure is so low that the lungs will not absorb the oxygen. It is at this altitude that a pressurized flight suit must be worn. Any altitude above 50,000 ft. is labeled as "space equivalent zone". pages.text: WB57 Missions Atmospheric Research Missions HDSS (High Definition Sounding System)/HIRAD (Hurricane Imaging Radiometer) Fall 2015 HDSS was a 100-hour flight campaign overflying Tropical Storm Marty (Pacific), Hurricane Joaquin (Atlantic: Cat 4), and Hurricane Patricia (Pacific: Cat 5) to collect very high resolution soundings of tropical cyclones with the intent of radically improving the understanding of tropical cyclones and the ability to predict their behavior. Significant accomplishments include: 1) most detailed set of tropical cyclone observations (including outflow, eyewall, eye, inflow) ever collected; 2) observations from 63,000 feet captured the entire structure of the storms for the first time; 3) observations were used in near-real time by the National Hurricane Center to refine official warnings. A total of 840 sondes were dropped into tropical cyclones during this campaign with a 99.5% success rate. VIRGAS (Volcano-plume Investigation Readiness and Gas-phase and Aerosol Sulfur) Fall 2015 VIRGAS was a multi-payload 30-hour airborne science flight campaign partially funded by the Upper Atmosphere Research Program (UARP) at NASA Headquarters. Sensors included the NOAA Water (H20), Sulfur Dioxide (SO2), and Ozone (O3) sensors, as well as NASA Ames and NCAR atmospheric measurement and sampling sensors. If plastic had been invented when the Pilgrims sailed from Plymouth, England, to North America—and the Mayflower had been stocked with bottled water and plastic-wrapped snacks—their plastic trash would likely still be around, four centuries later. If the Pilgrims had been like many people today and simply tossed their empty bottles and wrappers over the side, Atlantic waves and sunlight would have worn all that plastic into tiny bits. And those bits might still be floating around the world’s oceans today, sponging up toxins to add to the ones already in them, waiting to be eaten by some hapless fish or oyster, and ultimately perhaps by one of us. We should give thanks that the Pilgrims didn’t have plastic, I thought recently as I rode a train to Plymouth along England’s south coast. I was on my way to see a man who would help me make sense of the whole mess we’ve made with plastic, especially in the ocean. After sheets of clear plastic trash have been washed in the Buriganga River, in Dhaka, Bangladesh, Noorjahan spreads them out to dry, turning them regularly— while also tending to her son, Momo. We need union recognition to safeguard our jobs Wed 18 Nov 2026 06.50 EST Last modified on Wed 18 Nov 2026 07.27 EST Share W hen I first got the call offering me a job at Rockstar, I was thrilled. I thought back to being a child and sneaking into my brother’s room to grab the PlayStation Portable so I could secretly play Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories. The same kid who fell in love with Rockstar’s games back then now gets to spend every day helping to create those worlds as an animation programmer at the studio in Edinburgh. This week, we will celebrate the culmination of more than a decade of effort: the release of the most anticipated game of all time, Grand Theft Auto VI . But our team has the opportunity to make history a second time this month. Right now, the ballot is open for Rockstar employees to decide whether we want the union we have built with our colleagues to get recognition. As someone who cares deeply about our team, cares about what we do, and wants us to be able to keep delivering world-class games into the future, I’m voting yes.

pages.text: We Sent a Cartographer to the Sale of One of America's Most Famous Maps | National Geographic By Nina Strochlic Published October 29, 2026 1:09 On a spring day in 1982, a never-before-sold piece went under the hammer at Christie's auction house in New York City. In a moment he later said left him breathless, Malcolm Forbes, Jr., the president of Forbes magazine, raised his paddle and won the hand-drawn survey of the Mason-Dixon Line for $360,000—the most ever spent on an American map at the time. The sale shocked bidders: As the price climbed to more than 20 times its estimated sale price, it also managed to overshadow a rare copy of the Declaration of Independence (which fetched $285,000). The losing bidder for the Mason-Dixon map was the Library of Congress. Forbes ended up with an unusual-looking relic: six sheets of paper conjoined into a manuscript just six and a half inches tall and over six feet long. It’s believed to be the only original copy of the western section of the Mason Dixon survey—the most famous border in America. ( Why Your Mental Map of the World Is (Probably) Wrong .) More than 40 years later, that same map has now sold for $1,187,500 to an anonymous buyer, according to Brunk Auctions in North Carolina. The bidding started at $400,000, a sale price that doubled within mere minutes. Today, the Mason-Dixon Line is synonymous with a divided America, and its darkest era. In the following, the term referent means the object which is referred to by a weak reference. A weak reference to an object is not enough to keep the object alive: when the only remaining references to a referent are weak references, garbage collection is free to destroy the referent and reuse its memory for something else. However, until the object is actually destroyed the weak reference may return the object even if there are no strong references to it. A primary use for weak references is to implement caches or mappings holding large objects, where it’s desired that a large object not be kept alive solely because it appears in a cache or mapping. For example, if you have a number of large binary image objects, you may wish to associate a name with each. If you used a Python dictionary to map names to images, or images to names, the image objects would remain alive just because they appeared as values or keys in the dictionaries. The WeakKeyDictionary and WeakValueDictionary classes supplied by the weakref module are an alternative, using weak references to construct mappings that don’t keep objects alive solely because they appear in the mapping objects. Damage and destruction of critical infrastructure When conflict takes place in urban settings, the compound effects on urban services is significant, albeit harder to quantify. Not only do communities face the damage and destruction of critical infrastructure, but efforts to repair and reconstruct are hindered by explosive hazards. Coastal areas typically have mild weather, while the interior has greater seasonal variation in temperature and precipitation. In Nome, yearly precipitation averages about 15 inches, and the average temperature is about 21 o F. Summers average around 50 o F. The first snow dusting of the year can fall as early as August, although heavy snowfall begins in October and will stay on the ground until May. Winter temperatures typically range from -10 to -20 o F, although it can reach as low as -65 o F, with an even lower windchill factor. With these extreme temperatures, the sea ice in the Bering and Chukchi Sea will freeze up around mid-October and remain frozen until breakup in late-May. Please see the W3C Graphics Activity statement to find out what W3C is currently doing and has already done in the area of Web Graphics, including SVG , WebCGM Profile , and PNG . Formats There is no limit in the Web specifications to the graphical formats that can be used on the Web. You just need a MIME type so that the format is labelled correctly for transfer across the Web, and so that a suitable viewer (if one exists) can be located at the other end. In practice, certain formats are more widely understood than others; certain formats are more suited to one type of graphical data than another; so you should make an informed choice about what format to use. The group plans to further improve interoperability across the Internet of Things (IoT) and address emerging use cases around physical AI. WoT counteracts fragmentation in IoT by providing building blocks that enable seamless integration of devices and services across the IoT ecosystem. Across domains like smart buildings, industrial automation, and energy management, it eliminates proprietary silos and significantly reduces integration effort. pages.text: Web Standards | W3C Skip to content Web Standards Web standards are blueprints –or building blocks– of a consistent and harmonious digitally connected world. The promise of web standards W3C standards define an open web platform for application development. The web has the unprecedented potential to enable developers to build rich interactive experiences, that can be available on any device. The platform continues to expand, but web users have long ago rallied around HTML as the cornerstone of the web. Many more technologies that W3C and its partners are creating extend the web and give it full strength, including CSS, SVG, WOFF, WebRTC, XML, and a growing variety of APIs. Read more about W3C Standards Why W3C web standards? W3C publishes recommendations, that are considered web standards. W3C web standards are optimized for interoperability, security, privacy, web accessibility, and internationalization. See the “what's new?” sections of CSS, XSL and Digital Publishing. What are style sheets? Style sheets describe how documents are presented on screens, in print, or perhaps how they are pronounced. W3C has actively promoted the use of style sheets on the Web since the Consortium was founded in 1994. The Style Activity has produced several W3C Recommendations (CSS1, CSS2, XPath, XSLT). CSS especially is widely implemented in browsers. By attaching style sheets to structured documents on the Web (e.g. HTML), authors and readers can influence the presentation of documents without sacrificing device-independence or adding new HTML tags . The easiest way to start experimenting with style sheets is to find a browser that supports CSS . Discussions about style sheets are carried out on the www-style@w3.org mailing list and on comp.­infosystems.­www.­authoring.­stylesheets . The W3C Style Activity is also developing XSL , which consists of a combination of XSLT and “Formatting Objects” (XSL-FO). Why two Style Sheet languages? Wondering which one to choose? pages.title: Web可持续发展 | 我们的使命 | W3C
pages.description: 本页面介绍Web可持续发展的重要意义，以及W3C在该领域开展的工作。
pages.text: Web可持续发展 | 我们的使命 | W3C 转到内容 Web可持续发展 技术若要实现可持续发展，必须将经济增长、社会福祉与环境保护融为一体。构建一个保护人类、地球与繁荣的可持续Web，是共建服务全人类Web的一部分。Web本是为人类而设计，但其技术却会对环境和更广泛的社会产生连锁影响。 用户担忧技术对生态造成的影响——无论是电子废弃物带来的影响，还是对发电与用电需求的增加，抑或是数据中心，再或是数字产品与服务产生的排放。各组织也比以往任何时候都更需要韧性。我们正在探讨数字产品和服务在设计、开发与运营方面如何能够减少对环境的负面影响，同时确保Web平台仍然是人们理想的空间。 我们与个人、设计师和开发者、软件和硬件厂商以及监管机构携手合作，推动多方积极参与W3C的工作，并尽己之力让Web更加可持续：一个对所有人开放、节约环境资源、支撑人与社会的Web。 W3C如何推进可持续发展 制定Web可持续发展指南 评估实施方案的可持续性影响 为创作者提供资源，助力实现Web可持续发展 协调可能影响Web未来可持续性的研发工作 支持Web可持续层面的教育与推广 与横向审阅小组协作，评估各项规范的可持续性影响 W3C可持续发展总监Tzviya Siegman阐释了数字可持续性的含义，并对《Web可持续发展指南》作了概要介绍。 可持续发展相关工作 Web可持续发展兴趣组 Web可持续发展兴趣组 的使命是提升数字可持续性，让Web更好地惠及全人类和地球。 该兴趣组的工作重点之一是制定W3C《Web可持续发展指南》及其配套的《影响评级》。小组的交付成果清单可在其 GitHub readme 上查阅。 Web可持续发展指南 W3C《Web可持续发展指南》 （Web Sustainability Guidelines简称WSG）旨在打造更有利于人类、地球和繁荣的数字产品。在实践中，这意味着减少数据、能源、处理和硬件的使用；让网站保持简洁、快速、无障碍和包容；减少浪费和不必要的第三方服务；并将可持续性纳入产品和业务决策。 WSG影响评级 W3C《Web可持续发展指南影响评级》 帮助团队了解哪些可持续性改进对人类、地球和繁荣的影响最大，以及实施这些改进的难度和耗时。每项指南均依据其潜在影响和预计实施周期进行评级，帮助组织明确优先发力方向。简而言之，它能帮助团队了解每项建议的潜在影响，并确定先着手推进哪些事项。 赞助支持 欢迎您所在的组织成为 “共享万维网”倡导者 ，该赞助机会对W3C会员和非会员均开放。 赞助此项工作 成为W3C会员，共建可持续Web W3C会员 携手 共建Web未来 。 欢迎 联系我们 ，了解 W3C会员权益 ，亲身参与其中，发挥重要作用！ Related content 欢迎参与 本页描述了个人和组织可以参与万维网联盟（W3C）工作，以推进Web标准化的方式。 页面 W3C可持续发展工作的相关新闻 筛选Web可持续发展相关新闻 新闻

pages.description: 本页面对Web安全进行了概括性的介绍。
pages.text: Web安全 | 我们的使命 | W3C 转到内容 Web安全 隐私和安全——作为 人权 和 公民自由 不可或缺的一部分——一直是Web联盟议程中的重要内容。例如，我们的工作在开发能够替代弱密码的身份验证技术、减少网络钓鱼和类似攻击威胁方面起到了关键作用。 然而，用户会合理地担心他们的个人数据被滥用以及在网上被追踪，包括浏览器指纹识别、虚假信息的传播和其他网络危害。这些都是困难且紧迫的挑战。我们已经开始讨论如何在不增加审查的情况下，帮助用户找到可信的Web内容。 2024年4月，Simone Onofri介绍W3C的安全标准化工作（时长00:09:46）。作为人权与公民自由的重要基石，隐私与安全始终是W3C的核心议程。在广岛召开的W3C成员会议上，Simone Onofri阐述了安全标准化战略的三大支柱：制定安全标准、建立验证机制、引导开发者构建安全可靠的web生态。 W3C如何处理安全问题 制定安全技术标准 审核Web标准的安全性 指导Web开发者以安全的方式进行设计和开发 制定安全标准 我们有几个小组专门制定安全标准。 威胁建模 威胁建模社区小组 为安全、隐私和用户权益保护专家以及技术领域专家提供了一个平台，用于创建威胁模型。这些模型是动态文档，识别跨领域的威胁和缓解措施，并提供有关剩余风险的信息。 Web应用安全 Web应用安全工作组 开发安全和策略机制，以提高Web应用的安全性，并实现安全的跨站点通信。 Web身份验证 Web身份验证工作组 定义了一个客户端API，为Web应用提供强身份验证功能。 联合身份认证 联合身份认证工作组 支持在不损害安全和隐私原则的情况下进行身份验证和授权流程。 Web支付安全 Web支付安全兴趣小组 致力于增强各种Web支付技术的安全性和互用性。 审查Web标准的安全性 安全审查由W3C团队协调的一组志愿审查员进行。我们欢迎更多人加入该团队。提出的问题使用 与PING相同的工具 进行跟踪。 我们正在组建一个小组，与安全研究人员和密码学家一起进行横向安全审查。 安全兴趣小组 (SING) 这个小组的使命是通过向制定标准的小组提供建议，指导他们如何避免和缓解技术上的安全问题，同时建议对现有标准和技术进行更改以提高安全性，从而改善Web的安全性。 指导Web开发者以安全的方式进行设计和开发 我们组建了一个跨组织小组，旨在为Web开发者提供指导并确保一种全方位的安全方法。 Web应用安全指南 Web应用安全指南（SWAG）社区小组 通过为Web开发者制定安全最佳实践，并为利益攸关方提供合作平台（例如OpenSSF、OWASP、Open Web Docs等），提高Web应用开发的整体安全性，从而使Web对用户来说更加安全。 小组正在制定 增强web应用程序安全性的开发指南 。 赞助安全标准化活动 欢迎您所在的单位成为“ W3C原则倡导者 ”；该赞助计划面向W3C成员与非成员单位开放。 赞助此项工作 成为W3C会员共建安全的Web W3C会员 在 塑造Web 的进程中发挥着重要作用。 联系W3C 以了解更多关于 W3C会员的权益 ，从而进一步发挥重要作用！

pages.text: Web标准 | W3C 转到内容 Web标准 Web标准作为蓝图或构建模块被用来构建一致且和谐的数字互联世界，这些标准应用到了浏览器、博客、搜索引擎及其他支持Web体验的软件中。 Web标准的承诺 W3C标准定义了一个 开放的Web平台 用于应用开发。Web拥有前所未有的潜能，使开发者能够构建丰富的、可以在任何设备上使用的互动体验。 Web平台不断扩展，实际上Web用户早已围绕HTML这个Web基石汇聚起来。W3C及其合作伙伴创建的更多技术扩展了Web并增强了其功能，包括CSS、SVG、WOFF、WebRTC、XML及越来越多的各种API。 了解W3C标准 为什么选择W3C发布的Web标准？ W3C发布的推荐标准被视为Web标准。 W3C根据 W3C标准化流程文档 制定技术规范，该流程旨在最大限度地达成共识、确保质量，并获得 W3C会员 及更广泛社区的认可和采纳。 W3C制定的Web标准在互操作性、安全性、隐私保护、Web无障碍和国际化层面进行了优化。 W3C经过验证的Web标准化流程基于公平、开放和免版税的原则，我们致力于打造一个所有人都可以使用的Web。 了解Web标准的潜力和承诺。 在W3C创建标准的价值 自1994年以来，W3C一直为创建Web标准提供一个高效的环境： 遵循基于共识的决策流程； 满足无障碍、隐私、安全性和国际化的要求； 反映各个行业和全球利益相关者的意见； 平衡速度、公平、公众责任和质量； 受益于参与者提供的 免版税专利许可承诺 ； 保持稳定持久（W3C确保标准发布的URI持续有效）； 受益于W3C内外各团体的广泛审查； 免费提供； 通过互用性测试得到强化。 广泛的应用范围 W3C的 标准、技术规范和指南 在Web上被广泛应用： 渲染网页； 任意设备均可以访问； Web的架构； 链接的数据和服务； 创作工具。 相关内容 W3C标准和草案 本页面列出了处于各个成熟度级别的W3C所有工作组的全部标准和规范。 目录 W3C的小组 该页面列出了W3C的各类工作小组。 目录 审阅与公众反馈 对规范、实现、测试套件和代码的公众评审与反馈。 页面

pages.text: Web標準 | W3C コンテンツへスキップ Web標準 Web標準は、一貫性があり調和のとれたデジタル接続された世界の青写真、あるいは構成要素です。ブラウザ、ブログ、検索エンジン、その他のソフトウェアに実装され、私たちのウェブ体験を支えています。 Web標準の約束 W3C 標準は、アプリケーション開発のための オープンなウェブプラットフォーム を定義しています。Webは、開発者がどのようなデバイスでも利用できるリッチなインタラクティブな経験を構築できる、前例のない可能性を秘めています。 プラットフォームは拡大し続けているが、ウェブ・ユーザーはとっくにHTMLをウェブの礎として結集しています。W3Cとそのパートナーは、CSS、SVG、WOFF、WebRTC、XML、そして増え続けるさまざまなAPIなど、ウェブを拡張し、ウェブの完全な強度を与える多くの技術を生み出しています。 W3C標準について詳しく読む なぜW3Cのウェブ標準なのか？ W3Cはウェブ標準とみなされる勧告を発表しています。 W3C は、 W3C プロセス に従って技術仕様を開発しています。このプロセスは、コンセンサスを最大化し、品質を保証し、 W3C 会員 やより広範なコミュニティによる支持と採用を得るように設計されています。 W3CのWeb標準は、相互運用性、セキュリティ、プライバシー、Webアクセシビリティ、国際化のために最適化されています。 W3C の実績あるWeb標準プロセスは、公平性、オープン性、ロイヤリティフリーに基づいており、すべての人のために Web を機能させています。 Web標準の持つ可能性と約束されたものについて学びましょう｡ W3Cで標準を作る価値 1994年以来、W3Cはウェブ標準を作成するための生産的な環境を提供してきました： 合意に基づく意思決定プロセスに従う アクセシビリティ、プライバシー、セキュリティ、国際化に対応する 多様な業界や世界中の利害関係者の意見を反映する 速度、公平性、公共の責任、品質のバランスをとる 参加者からの ロイヤリティフリーの特許ライセンスのコミットメント の恩恵を受ける 安定しており（W3Cは発行されたURIでの持続性を保証する） W3C内外のグループから広範なレビューを受ける 無料で利用可能 相互運用性テストを通じて強化される 幅広い用途 W3C 標準、技術仕様、およびガイドライン は、ウェブ上で広く展開されています： Web ページのレンダリング あらゆるデバイスからのアクセスが可能 Webのアーキテクチャ データとサービスのリンク オーサリングツール 参考 W3C の標準と草稿 このページでは、あらゆる成熟度レベルの、あらゆるW3C作業部会による、すべてのW3C標準と仕様をリストアップしています。 ディレクトリー一覧 W3CのWeb標準について このページでは、ワールド・ワイド・ウェブ・コンソーシアムでオープンなウェブ標準を作成することの価値など、W3Cのウェブ標準について詳しく説明します。 ページ レビューと公開フィードバック 仕様、実装、テスト・スイート、コードに関する公開レビューとフィードバック。 ページ 私たちの使命 W3Cとは何か、W3Cの価値観、そして、ウェブの可能性を最大限に引き出すというW3Cの使命に基づく原則についてご紹介します。 ページ

Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Weeds and Invasives The BLM manages 245 million acres of public lands primarily in the Western United States, including Alaska. Seventy-nine million of these acres are impacted by noxious and invasive weeds. One of the BLM's highest priorities is to promote ecosystem health and one of the greatest obstacles to achieving this goal is the rapid expansion of weeds across public lands. These invasive plants can dominate and often cause permanent damage to natural plant communities. If not eradicated or controlled, noxious weeds will continue to jeopardize the health of the public lands and to constrain the myriad activities that occur on public lands. About Weeds and Invasives The term "weed" means different things to different people. In the broadest sense, it is any plant growing where it is not wanted. Weeds can be native or non-native, invasive or non invasive, and noxious or not noxious. Learn more and review Frequently Asked Questions .
